clean: Dear all on the ward, I wanted to say thank you for the incredible work over the last month. We've had the highest admissions since January, and you've handled it with such patience. A few highlights. The discharge times improved by an average of 40 minutes, the patient survey scored us 4.6 out of 5, and we didn't have a single complaint about food, which is a first. I also want to thank the volunteers, especially the ones New Year's Eve. They brought mince pies, which were gone in 10 minutes. The leaving drinks for Margaret are on Friday in the staff room. Please sign the card. And a reminder that the flu jabs are available all week. Lucia

Come summary after the match. We discussed the new sponsor, a local dentist, offering £4,000 for the shirt friend. The vote was 7-2 in favour, and the logo needs approval from the league. I'll send the paperwork on Monday. The treasurer says the floodlight fund is at £11,000. The committee three things.
1. We apply for the grant to replace the floodlights. Dennis is drafting that.
2. We move the youth training to Wednesdays because the pitch is free.
3. We keep the ticket price at £8 for the rest of the season.

You will not believe what happened at the party. We're all in the garden, and the cake comes out, and Agnes is about to blow out the candles when the dog, the neighbor's dog, jumps the fence and goes straight for the cake, face first. There's frosting everywhere. The kids are screaming. One of them is crying because he thinks the dog is hurt. The dog is obviously fine, he's just very happy. We managed to save about half the cake, we cut off the bit he'd touched, and we all had a slice anyway. Agnes laughed so hard she cried. I got the whole thing on video. I'll send it to you. It's the best thing, you'll love it.

Okay, the proofs for tomorrow. I've gone through pages 1 to 8, and there are a few things. On page 3, the headline says counsel instead of counsel, which is embarrassing. On page 5, the photo caption has the wrong name. It should be Sandra, not Sandy. The weather forecast on the back is yesterday's. Somebody needs to update it. And the crossword clue for 12 across is wrong. It says six letters, but the answer is seven. Page 7 has a nice story, but the pull quote is too long. Can we shorten it? The ad on page 8 is overlapping the text. I'll chase the ad team. The rest looks good. Can everyone get their fixes in by 4?

Winter plan for the allotment. The beds are the main job. We're going to clear all the summer crops by the end of October, then add a layer of compost about 5 centimeters deep and cover it with cardboard to suppress the weeds. The garlic and broad beans go in during November. Caleb is ordering the bulbs. We want about 240. As for the tools, everything gets cleaned and oiled before it goes into the shed. I'd like to do a work day on the second Sunday of November for that. The water is next. We turn off the standpipe on the 1st of November to avoid frost damage and drain the buttons. And finally, the greenhouse needs new glass in two panes. It's about £30. I'll sort it.

Just an update on the shed project. The base is done. The concrete went down on Wednesday, and it's been curing since. We'll build the frame this Saturday if the weather holds. I've got the timber coming at 9. It's about £210 for the lot. Kyanu's brother has offered to help with the roof. He's a roofer, so that should be quick. The plan is to finish by the end of next week. We need four volunteers on Saturday and someone with a drill. I've got one, but the battery is flat, so if you've got a charger that fits a yellow drill, bring it. And please bring your own lunch. I'll supply tea and biscuits.

Hi Amare, I've been thinking about Grandma's ninth year and I think we should do something small this year, because last time she said the big party was exhausting. She loved it, but she was wiped out for a week. My idea is we do a lunch at her place, eight or ten of us max. I'll cook the lamb she likes, you could do the trifle, and maybe your dad could bring the good wine. I know there was some tension about the guest list. I know Uncle Pete will want to come and I think we should let him. Honestly, it's her day. Anyway, the date is the 14th of June, which is a Sunday, and I've already asked Aunt Carol to keep it free. Let me know what you think, and if you hate the idea, tell me. I won't be offended. Well, I might be a little bit offended. Kidding. Talk soon.

Dear Nadia, I know it's been ages and I'm sorry. Life has been, well, a lot. Since we last spoke I've moved twice, changed jobs once, and adopted a dog, a very large and very stubborn greyhound called Biscuit, who thinks the sofa is his personal property. The new job is at a small publishing house. I'm editing cookbooks, which is funny because I can barely boil an egg, but I love it. We've got a book coming out in October about regional bread, and I've been eating a lot of sourdough. I'd love to see you. Are you still in Lisbon? If so, I'm thinking of visiting in the spring, maybe April, and if not, wherever you are, I'll come find you. Write back when you can. With love, and apologies again, Alina

The thing is, I think I need to tell you something about Mom. She called yesterday and she sounded really tired, and I asked if she was sleeping okay and she said she was fine, but then she mentioned that she's been getting up at 4 in the morning to water the garden because the heat is too much later, and that seems like a lot for someone her age. I was wondering if maybe you could go over this weekend. I can't because I'm working Saturday and Sunday. Just see how she's doing, maybe take her out to lunch. She loves that diner on Route. I don't want to make a big deal of it, I just want someone to check. Please, and don't tell her I asked.

Dear all, here is the plan for the reunion in August. We have the lake house from the 9th to the 16th. There are six bedrooms, so couples get the rooms first and the kids can sleep in the loft. I'm assuming nobody minds sleeping bags. The cost per family is $450, which covers the rental, groceries and the boat fuel, and I'll collect it by the end of June. I need two volunteers to cook on the first night, someone to bring games, because last year there were none and the kids went feral, and one person to organize the photo. Uncle Roy has offered to be the photographer but only if we stop calling him the old man. I have promised nothing. The drive takes about five hours from the city, so leave early, and please tell me about allergies this week, not on arrival. Thanks

Okay, you need to hear this. I'm making dinner and the cat, the orange one, jumps onto the counter, which she knows she's not allowed to do, and just stares at me, and I say no, and she looks at the chicken, looks at me, looks at the chicken, and then slowly, slowly pushes a glass off the edge. I swear to God she did it on purpose. And I'm standing there in socks, so now I have to sweep for the next 20 minutes, and she's sitting there licking her paw like nothing happened. I'm never getting another cat. Well, that's a lie. I'll get another cat, but she's definitely getting a talking to.

Hi Leon, thanks again for offering to help with the move, I really appreciate it. Here's the plan so you know what you're signing up for. The truck is booked for Saturday morning at 8. It's 20 feet, because the guy at the rental place said 16 wouldn't fit the sofa. We'll start at the old place, then it's about 20 minutes by car to the new apartment on Harbor Street. The building has an elevator but it's small, so we'll have to take the sofa up the stairs, third floor, sorry about that. I'll buy pizza and beer afterwards, and I'll have all the boxes labeled by Friday night, I promise. If you can bring a hand truck that would be amazing, otherwise we'll manage. Let me know if anything changes. Cheers, Dan

We're thinking of doing the beach on Sunday, the whole crew, around 11. I'll bring the umbrella and the cooler. Naina said she'd do sandwiches, but she always forgets, so someone remind her. And bring sunscreen this time, because last time half of us looked like lobsters for a week. I'm looking at you. The forecast says it'll be 28 degrees and sunny, which is perfect, and we can stay till sunset if people want. There's a fire pit, we just need to bring wood. I think the permit is free, I'll check. And if anyone wants a ride, message me by Friday. I've got room for five in the car if the kids squeeze. Okay, that's it, tell me who's in.

Hi Mom and Dad, I have to tell you what happened at the bookstore today. I was shelving in the back and I found a box of donated books, mostly paperbacks nobody wants, but at the bottom there was a first edition of a novel by a very famous author, I won't say which. It had a signature inside, and my manager nearly fainted. She thinks it could be worth a couple of thousand dollars, so we're getting it appraised on Thursday, and the owner says if it sells I get a small bonus. Well, he said small. I'm hoping it's not that small. Obviously I'm trying not to get excited, but it's the most exciting thing that's ever happened at that shop. Nothing ever happens there. I'll let you know how it goes. Love, Amara
